Joyeux anniversaire,

Wangechi

Your table is set at —

Happy birthday, my love.

If you asked me how many times you came into my mind,
I would say once — because you came, and never left.

All roads lead to you,
even the ones I took to forget you.

You are killing me, and you are keeping me from dying.
That is love.

If a thousand others loved you,
their love would be a drop against my ocean.

They asked, “Do you love her to death?”
I said, “Speak of her over my grave,
and watch how she brings me back to life.”

I used to dream of drinking tea with you at night,
of being partners in happiness, in joy.

Believe me, my dear, it warms my heart even when you are far —
not because I love you less, but because I love you more.

A university degree, four books, hundreds of articles,
and still I misread you: you wrote “Good morning,”
and I read it as “I love you.”

Mahmoud Darwish
